context.text: Alignment in Aethel

Alignment in Decennium Descent is a fundamental aspect of a character's moral compass and worldview, significantly impacting interactions and alliances. It is not merely a label but a core mechanic influencing reputation and party dynamics. Aethel recognizes a nine-point alignment system that combines moral outlook (Good, Neutral, Evil) with ethical approach (Lawful, Neutral, Chaotic).
The Nine Alignments
Detailed Alignment Descriptions

You can't hide from a creature that can see you clearly, and if you make noise (such as shouting a warning or knocking over a vase), you give away your position. An invisible creature can't be seen, so it can always try to hide. Signs of its passage might still be noticed, however, and it still has to stay quiet. In combat, most creatures stay alert for signs of danger all around, so if you come out of hiding and approach a creature, it usually sees you. However, under certain circumstances, the Director might allow you to stay hidden as you approach a creature that is distracted, allowing you to gain advantage on an attack roll before you are seen.

Passive Perception. When you hide, there's a chance someone will notice you even if they aren't searching. To determine whether such a creature notices you, the Director compares your Dexterity (Stealth) check with that creature's passive Wisdom (Perception) score, which is 10 + the creature's Wisdom modifier, as well as any other bonuses or penalties. If the creature has advantage, add 5. For disadvantage, subtract 5.
For example, if a 1st-level character (with a proficiency bonus of +2) has a Wisdom of 15 (a +2 modifier) and proficiency in Perception, he or she has a passive Wisdom (Perception) of 14.

context.text: Chapter 5 — Creating Adventures and Expedition Arcs
An "adventure" in Decennium Descent is rarely a single dungeon crawl — it's an arc across some slice of an Opening, built from a hook, an obstacle, and a consequence that seeds the next arc.

Where hooks come from. The strongest hooks in this setting are never "a wizard needs an errand." They come from the machine's own appetite: a rumor that a Custodian's private ledger survived on Floor 44; a rival Expedition's disastrous return with an item everyone now wants; a faction offering absurd money for something specific, for reasons they won't explain; a haven under siege from something that came up from a floor rather than in from the wilds. Loot-as-bait means your hooks can honestly be about greed — the world is built to make greed reasonable.
Three shapes of arc.

hits.text: The Player Rulebook treats Good and Evil characters as unable to form a stable Expedition together. Enforce that rule during character creation rather than discovering the conflict after play begins. Neutral characters may bridge moral differences, but the table still needs agreement on methods. context.text: Alignment Compatibility

The Player Rulebook treats Good and Evil characters as unable to form a stable Expedition together. Enforce that rule during character creation rather than discovering the conflict after play begins. Neutral characters may bridge moral differences, but the table still needs agreement on methods. Alignment does not excuse one player from respecting another player’s boundaries.
Horror Through Choice

Describe enough for players to understand risk, then let them choose how closely to engage. A sealed corpse may be investigated through medical detail, religious rite, distant tools, or not at all. Horror becomes stronger when the group chooses to look rather than being trapped in unwanted description.

Wounds

Hit points represent endurance, luck, armor deflection, and minor injury. Wounds represent lasting trauma. A creature makes a Wound save when it drops to 0 HP, suffers damage equal to at least half its maximum HP from one source, or is struck by an effect marked Maiming. The save is Constitution, DC 10 or half the triggering damage, whichever is higher.
